top_story: The Houthi strike on Riyadh airport on 10 October, followed by another hit on 11 October, marks a sharp escalation in Yemen’s war as the group demonstrated an ability to sustain attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure, killing 13 people and injuring more than 300. That escalation now intersects more openly with the wider Iran confrontation after London judged a plot targeting a British airbase used by US forces was almost certainly directed by the Revolutionary Guards, tightening the link between Gulf insecurity and extra-regional military risk. The same conflict environment is also driving a severe human toll beyond the battlefield, underscored by the 11 October boat disaster off Djibouti in which at least 139 migrants died while trying to reach Yemen despite its active war zone. The regional picture is one of interconnected militarisation and desperation, with proxy confrontation expanding across borders as civilians absorb the deadliest consequences.
